catalogue.notes:
DATA SOURCE: live production database, read via the authenticated admin UI at https://kclinics.co.uk (RSC payloads of /admin/services, /admin/staff, /admin/devices, /admin/bookings, logged in with the QA admin account). Direct Postgres access failed: the sandbox egress proxy blocks the Neon DB host (TCP 5432 and SQL-over-HTTP both denied, "Host not in allowlist"), so the Prisma script route was impossible. This is NOT seed data — it is the same listServices(includeInactive=true) query the admin Services & Pricing page runs. Note: QA_ADMIN_PASSWORD has trailing whitespace in the env; it must be .trim()ed before use.

CATALOGUE: 37 services, 172 variants, all included, prices in pence as stored. All services are category "aesthetics" (no dentistry rows). Complete: no truncation.

ANOMALIES: (1) costPence is null on ALL 172 variants — the clinic has never entered cost of goods, so margins must be modelled from assumptions. (2) No zero-price variants; "on consultation" is expressed via status instead: lhr-women and spider-veins have service status CONSULTATION (price shown but booking goes via consultation). COMING_SOON (not yet sold): intimate-rejuvenation, fungal-nail, laser-tattoo-removal, pmu-removal. Three services are inactive (hidden): carbon-laser-peel, caci, red-carpet-lift — marked in their status field since the schema had no service-level active property. (3) Per-variant active flag is not serialized by the admin page (lib/services.ts toVariant drops it), so inactive variants are present but indistinguishable; variant-level status overrides ARE included (almost all null). (4) Duplicate Botox service (slugs botox-j2j7 and botox-r9w5, identical variants/prices) and overlapping face-treatments/vacuum-massage services — dedupe before revenue modelling. (5) displayDurationMin is the client-facing time; durationMin is the internal room-blocking time (setup+treatment+clean) — use durationMin for capacity modelling.

VAT PICTURE: only "Laser Hair Removal — Women" has an explicit vatClass (EXEMPT); the other 36 services are null, which the app derives as STANDARD for aesthetics (dentistry would derive EXEMPT, but there are none). So effectively: everything standard-rated 20% except women's LHR flagged exempt — that exemption looks questionable for a cosmetic LHR service (UK VAT exemption needs a medical purpose) and its men's counterpart is standard, so treat it as a data-entry inconsistency worth flagging, not a tax fact.

ROOMS: 11 active ROOM resources (from the devices page query: kind=ROOM, active=true): 3 Aesthetics, 2 Dental, 6 Treatment. Inactive rooms, floors and tags were not exposed via this route.

STAFF: 14 AdminUser rows total. Active: 3 OWNER (one is the Claude QA bot, one is Joe the developer — arguably 1 real operating owner, Inna), 1 ADMIN (receptionist Tetiana), 1 PRACTITIONER (Hanna S), 1 FRONT_DESK (shared info account). Plus 8 inactive PRACTITIONER accounts that are clearly test data (doctor1-5@gmail.com etc.). Realistic operating headcount for the model: 1 owner, 1 receptionist/admin, 1 clinician.

BOOKING VOLUME: counted from the admin bookings list, which filters on appointment date (startAt), NOT createdAt — createdAt-based counting was not reachable through any accessible endpoint, so "last 90 days" means startAt >= 2026-05-30. Total ever = 486 (261 with startAt up to Feb 2026 — imported historical records with legacy titles like "Back of Neck 6 session"; zero Mar 1–May 29 2026, the pre-reopening gap; 225 since May 30, of which 34 are future-dated upcoming appointments). byTreatment covers the 225 recent bookings, mapped from display titles to treatment slugs (heuristic; "consultation" includes generic and LHR consultations; small naming variances possible between cosmetic-injections/injectables and microcurrent/microcurrent-facial, rf-lifting/rf-skin-tightening). Demand is dominated by laser hair removal (~63% of recent non-consultation bookings). One "Ultimate Skin Membership" product also appears in historical bookings (9 rows) — a membership revenue line exists historically.

Scripts used (scratchpad): extract.mjs (Prisma attempt, blocked), extract-http.mjs (Neon HTTP attempt, blocked), scrape.mjs (working admin scrape), agg.mjs (90d treatment aggregation). Raw scrape saved at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-K-Clinics/051a7c64-a236-5eff-95a6-24669350257f/scratchpad/scrape.json.

context.notes:
Room/staff structure: no fixed room count or floor area anywhere in the repo. Rooms and equipment are DB-configured resource pools (lib/availability.ts); a settings toggle decides whether machines are tied to specific rooms or treated as movable units ('limited only by how many units you own' — lib/settings.ts). docs/BOOKING_ARCHITECTURE.md describes the original 'one treatment room model' (a slot is taken if any booking overlaps), since extended to clinician + room + equipment pools — so for the financial model, capacity = min(clinicians, rooms, machine units) per modality. The staff manual mentions per-room display screens but no headcount.

Pricing architecture already in place (relevant to the model):
- Courses/packages: laser hair removal courses of 3/6/10 at reduced per-session rates (15% offer); RF course of 3 £690 / 5 £1075; HIFU courses of 3; Endosphere 3 £300 / 6 £540 / 10 £800. lib/services.ts (BLD-1268): each ServiceVariant carries configured package/course tiers — packages are structural in the catalogue, not ad-hoc.
- Named bundles (RESEARCH.md): BodyContour (6x Endosphere + 6x vacuum), Ultimate Hair-Free (women), Total Rejuvenation, Perfect Skin, Smooth & Slim.
- Tiered single service: HydraFacial three tiers £95/£145/£185 (price ladder inside one machine).
- Offers/loyalty: 15% off first visit (dental or aesthetic), free consultations, 'Beauty Points' loyalty scheme. No membership/subscription scheme found.
- Payment mechanics: card-on-file (Stripe SetupIntent), charged only on delivery; 100% late-cancel fee inside 24h (waivable) — protects utilisation revenue. 'On consultation' items book as £0 holds with staff-set charge.
- Prices are 'from' prices per area; the admin catalogue (Service → ServiceVariant) is the single source of truth, PRICE_LIST.md (docs) is the authoritative snapshot. Dentistry has no price sheet yet.
- Capex pipeline signal: tattoo-removal/PMU/spider-vein laser and the microcurrent/LED/facial-massage menu are onRequest ('machine not in yet') — pages and prices exist, so the model can treat these as a phase-2 machine purchase with pre-validated price points. Dentistry (chair, imaging, GDC dentist, separate company) is the other deferred investment; dentistryLive: false.
- Highest-ticket aesthetics: CO2 intimate treatments (£690), HIFU full face & neck (£559), men's full body LHR (£321). Injectables COGS: fat-dissolving £150/vial.
Key files: /home/user/K-Clinics/lib/treatments.ts, /home/user/K-Clinics/lib/treatments-imported.ts, /home/user/K-Clinics/lib/site.ts, /home/user/K-Clinics/docs/PRICE_LIST.md, /home/user/K-Clinics/docs/RESEARCH.md, /home/user/K-Clinics/docs/BOOKING_ARCHITECTURE.md, /home/user/K-Clinics/lib/availability.ts.

findings.item: Business electricity unit rate, UK small business (Aug 2026)
findings.unit: p/kWh (ex VAT for CCL-registered; small businesses pay 20% VAT unless usage <33 kWh/day)
findings.basis: Comparison-site market data for August 2026: AquaSwitch/BusinessEnergyDeals quote ~29.6p/kWh average for a small business; Bionic/Expertsure put competitive fixed rates at 20-23p/kWh and typical real-world rates 22-30p/kWh. Use 25-27p/kWh as a central planning figure for a micro business on a 2026 fixed deal.

findings.item: Business electricity standing charge, UK small business (Aug 2026)
findings.basis: BusinessEnergyDeals/AquaSwitch August 2026 data: average daily standing charge ~55.3p for small businesses, supplier range 34.7p-105.9p/day (adds roughly £125-£387/yr).

findings.item: Ofgem domestic price cap electricity (cross-check), 1 Jul - 30 Sep 2026
findings.unit: p/kWh inc 5% VAT, plus 57.19p/day standing charge
findings.basis: Ofgem price cap for 1 July - 30 September 2026 (GB average, Direct Debit): 26.11p/kWh electricity, 57.19p/day standing charge; typical annual dual-fuel bill £1,663. Confirms the ~26-30p/kWh business range is realistic.

findings.item: Business gas unit rate, UK small business (Aug 2026)
findings.unit: p/kWh, plus gas standing charge ~25-60p/day for a micro business
findings.basis: MoneySuperMarket Aug 2026: business gas unit rates 7.9-8.2p/kWh by size; AquaSwitch indicative micro-business fixed rates 4-5p/kWh; general small-business range 7-12p/kWh. Ofgem domestic cap cross-check: 7.33p/kWh + 29.04p/day (Jul-Sep 2026). Note: a small leased unit in a converted Clerkenwell building like 4 Charterhouse Buildings very often has NO gas supply - CIBSE TM46 assigns 'general retail' zero fossil-thermal, i.e. all-electric heating (reverse-cycle split A/C or panel heaters) is the typical small-commercial approach; model heating on the electricity tariff unless a gas meter is confirmed.

findings.item: Cooling energy benchmark, small conditioned commercial space
findings.unit: kWh/m2/yr electricity for cooling (concentrated May-Sep; roughly 0.2-0.5 kWh/m2/day in summer months, near zero Nov-Mar)
findings.basis: CIBSE (CIBSE Journal, citing UK air-conditioning studies): cooling in offices typically ~40 kWh/m2/yr; a treatment room with laser/RF plant heat gain sits at or above office levels. For a monthly curve, put ~80-90% of it in May-September.

findings.item: Heating energy benchmark, small commercial/clinical space
findings.unit: kWh/m2/yr delivered heat (electric heat pump input ~ divide by COP 2.5-3.5; concentrated Oct-Apr)
findings.basis: CIBSE TM46:2008 benchmarks: general office fossil-thermal typical 120 kWh/m2/yr; general retail 165 kWh/m2/yr electricity total with 0 fossil-thermal (all-electric assumption). CIBSE Guide A/F: good-practice office thermal ~114, typical ~210 kWh/m2/yr. For a small well-insulated clinic heated by reverse-cycle splits, ~50-120 kWh/m2/yr delivered heat, so ~20-45 kWh/m2/yr of electricity at COP ~3.

CIBSE TM46:2008 'General retail' typical electricity benchmark 165 kWh/m2/yr (all-electric, includes heating/cooling/lighting/equipment). For a ~80-120 m2 clinic that implies ~13,000-20,000 kWh/yr - consistent with Ofgem's micro-business band.

findings.item: Split A/C for a 15-20 m2 treatment room: rated cooling capacity
findings.basis: UK installer sizing guides (Daikin UK, Glow Green, CoolEasy, 2026): 15 m2 room needs 2.5-3.0 kW, 20 m2 needs 3.0-3.5 kW cooling output; add a step for laser/IPL plant heat gain.

findings.item: Split A/C electrical input draw, 15-20 m2 room
findings.unit: kW electrical input while running (inverter units modulate; average duty draw is often half of peak)
findings.basis: UK 2026 running-cost guides (Be Cool Refrigeration, Hamilton Aircon, Selectra): a good inverter split delivers 3.5 kW cooling from ~0.5-1.0 kW input (SEER 3.5-7); running cost quoted at 7-15p/hr for an efficient unit up to ~35-50p/hr worst case at 2026 rates. Typical clinic run hours: 6-10 h/day on treatment days in summer, so ~3-8 kWh/room/day cooling in July-August, near zero in winter (or reversed for heating).

findings.item: Lighting + base load (fridge, autoclave/sterilizer, PCs, screens, router), small clinic
findings.basis: Derived from Ofgem/Bionic micro-business consumption band (5,000-15,000 kWh/yr = 14-41 kWh/day all-in) minus HVAC share, and bottom-up: LED lighting ~5-8 W/m2 x 100 m2 x 10 h = 5-8 kWh; benchtop autoclave ~1.5-2 kW x 3-6 cycles ~ 2-4 kWh; med/skincare fridge ~0.5-1 kWh; 3-4 PCs/screens/kiosk ~1.5-3 kWh; towel warmer/kettle/misc 1-3 kWh. Central estimate ~12 kWh/day non-HVAC, treatment machines excluded.

research.notes: Rates found via August 2026 comparison-site data and the Ofgem Jul-Sep 2026 domestic cap (the cap does not apply to business supply but is a good cross-check; business unit rates run 0-4p above it, and small businesses without CCL relief pay 20% VAT vs the domestic 5%). Key modelling caveat: 4 Charterhouse Buildings is likely all-electric (TM46 treats general retail as zero fossil-thermal), so build heating into the electricity tariff via reverse-cycle splits at COP ~3 unless a gas meter is confirmed on the lease. Seasonal curve suggestion: cooling 40 kWh/m2/yr weighted ~Jun 20%, Jul 30%, Aug 30%, May/Sep 15%, rest ~5%; heating (delivered) 50-120 kWh/m2/yr weighted Dec-Feb ~55%, Nov/Mar ~30%, Oct/Apr ~15%. Treatment-machine (laser/IPL/RF) consumption is NOT in finding 10 and should be modelled separately per device duty cycle.

findings.item: Diode laser hair removal — purchase NEW
findings.basis: UK trade listings: clinic-grade diode £8k–£15k (thelasermachineco.co.uk, britishlasers.com); premium platforms (Alma Soprano Titanium, Candela GentleMax Pro, Cynosure Elite+) £30k–£60k. Typical premium-clinic buy ~£18k–£35k.

findings.item: Diode laser hair removal — useful life & capacity
findings.basis: Industry standard: diode stacks rated 1M+ shots; depreciate over 5–7 yrs. Capacity ~10–14 treatments/day (20–60 min each), ~2,500/yr at full utilisation.

findings.item: Diode laser hair removal — power draw & effective energy
findings.basis: Plate rating 2.0–3.5 kW; laser fires ~25–40% of treatment time (duty cycle) → effective ~0.6–1.5 kWh/hr. Estimate from manufacturer specs (Soprano Titanium 3.6 kW max).

findings.item: Diode laser hair removal — service & consumables
findings.basis: UK service houses (britishlasers.com, UK Laser Group): annual contract typically 5–10% of purchase; consumables = ultrasound gel + razors ~£1–£2/session.
Lumenis Stellar M22 new ~£45k–£70k (US listings $60k–$90k); Lynton Lumina (UK-built, Motus-class) ~£28k–£50k depending on handpiece set. If bought as combi unit with diode, shares chassis cost.
Industry standard for premium platforms; IPL flashlamps are the wear item (~50k–100k pulses per lamp). Capacity ~8–12 treatments/day across indications.
Plate 1.5–3 kW; pulsed operation with capacitor charging, duty ~25–35% → ~0.5–1.2 kWh/hr effective. Estimate from Lumenis/Lynton specs.

findings.value: 3000 service/yr; 2 consumables/session; lamp replacement 500–1500 per handpiece
findings.basis: Lynton/Lumenis UK contracts typically £2k–£5k/yr (6–8% of price); consumables gel £1–£2/session; periodic IPL lamp/handpiece refurb.

research.notes: Confidence tiers: purchase prices for diode, pico, HIFU, HydraFacial, dental, PRP and microneedling are anchored to published UK/US listings; Endospheres, CACI, MonaLisa Touch/FemiLift and Morpheus8 are dealer-quote-only in the UK, so those are estimates from dealer channels and international listings (marked in basis). Power draw and duty cycle are engineering estimates from manufacturer plate ratings — no supplier publishes kWh-per-treatment figures; the effective kWh/treatment-hour values assume the stated duty cycles and are suitable for a cost model but are the least-sourced numbers here. Energy cost impact is small in every case: at ~30p/kWh even the heaviest laser costs under £0.50/treatment-hour in electricity — consumables and service dominate running cost, especially HIFU cartridges, Morpheus8 tips and HydraFacial serums. For a model: use straight-line depreciation over the life values, service at 6% of capex/yr for lasers and 4% for non-laser electromechanical, and finance at ~£205/month per £10k over 5 years (or 4.2%/yr implicit-interest add-on). The pico laser and dental packages are flagged NOT YET PURCHASED / NOT LIVE in the task — figures given are for the acquisition case.

corporationTax.basis: 2026/27 rates; marginal relief makes each £ between £50k–£250k effectively 26.5%. A startup-year clinic will almost certainly be in the 19% band.

aia.note: Annual Investment Allowance: 100% first-year TAX deduction on qualifying plant & machinery (all lasers/devices/fit-out; full expensing also available on new main-rate plant). TIMING benefit only — the accounting P&L still depreciates machinery straight-line over the life-years in the machinery table (4–9 yrs). MODEL TAX AND BOOK DEPRECIATION SEPARATELY: expect tax losses / minimal CT in the capex year, deferred-tax style divergence after.

tax.employmentAllowance: Up to £10,500/yr offset against employer NI if eligible — worth ~the full NI bill at this headcount.

gaps: COGS: costPence is null on ALL 172 catalogue variants — every consumablesGBP figure in the treatments table is an assumption from supplier research, not a recorded cost. Highest sensitivity: HIFU cartridges (£30–£100/session; £300–£900 if Ultherapy-brand), HydraFacial serums (contract-tied), and all injectable vial/syringe costs (brand unknown — toxin and filler brands not recorded anywhere).
Floor area & rent: no sqft anywhere in the codebase. Rent placeholder (£64k = 2,000 sqft x £32) and HVAC room size (15 m2/room) are pure assumptions — get the actual lease and floor plan.
Business rates: rateable value unknown — check VOA for 4 Charterhouse Buildings; outcome ranges from £0 (SBRR if RV≤£12k) to ~£15k+.

Machine ownership unverified for three classes: CO2 laser (intimate line COMING_SOON — owned or planned capex?), microcurrent/LED device (code says 'not yet in', catalogue and 6 bookings say otherwise), and the exact brands/purchase prices of the owned diode, IPL, HIFU, RF, Endosphere and HydraFacial units (all machinery capex figures are class-typical, not invoices).
Pico laser capex spans £12.5k–£175k depending on tier — a decision, not an estimate; tattoo/PMU revenue upside is pre-priced but gated on it.
Endosphere, CACI, CO2-gynae and Morpheus-class purchase prices are dealer-quote-only in the UK (no published list prices) — lowest-confidence capex figures.

kWh-per-treatment-hour values are engineering estimates from plate ratings and assumed duty cycles — no manufacturer publishes them. Financial impact is small (<£0.50/treatment-hour) so precision is not required.
Gas supply unconfirmed — model assumes all-electric (TM46 convention for converted commercial); a gas meter on the lease would change the heating tariff from 27p to ~7p/kWh.

Demand/ramp: only 90 days of post-reopening bookings (225, startAt-based proxy — createdAt was unreachable), ~2.5/day against 9-room capacity; no conversion-rate, retention, or course-uptake data. The revenue ramp and course-vs-single mix (courses discount ~15%) are the model's dominant free assumptions.

Course pricing inconsistencies in the live catalogue: Laser Skin Resurfacing 5-session course (£450) is cheaper than the 3-session (£480); tattoo-removal Small shares course totals with Very Small. Fix before publishing a pricing architecture.

Duplicate/overlapping services in the DB: botox-r9w5 duplicates botox-j2j7 (excluded here); Red Carpet Lift BB Glow duplicates the BB Glow service; three inactive services (carbon-laser-peel, caci, red-carpet-lift) carry prices — confirm intended state. Per-variant active flags are not serialized by the admin page, so some included variants may actually be off.

VAT: women's-LHR EXEMPT flag treated as a data error (modelled 20%) — needs owner/accountant sign-off; VAT registration date is a modelling switch with no set date; energy VAT rate (5% vs 20%) depends on the de-minimis 33 kWh/day test.
Owner remuneration and developer/platform maintenance time are unmodelled labour costs — both need explicit assumptions.
Membership: an 'Ultimate Skin Membership' appears in 9 historical bookings but no current membership product or price exists — recurring-revenue line is a design decision, not an input.
Dental: entirely excluded from the base model (not live, separate company, no price sheet) — the £70k single-surgery capex figure is carried only as a deferred-scenario input.
Dental rooms: 2 of the 11 rooms are dental-fitted and unusable for aesthetics — base-case capacity uses 9 rooms; confirm they are not being used as overflow treatment rooms.
